entities.text: Chitra Agarwal Vs. M/s. Cubs International Prtrochem Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the opposite party had entered into a transaction with the company namely, M/s.
Castle Industries Private Limited and the opposite party had raised invoices pertaining to the supply of products in the name of the said company.
Out of total alleged outstanding amount of Rs. 24,02,546/-, the accused company being M/s.

Castle Industries Private Limited had released certain amount and paid to the complainant/opposite party and thereafter, the complainant has stated that the accused person failed to release purported sum of Rs. 10,25,745/-.

The complainant thereafter has stated that the accused person failed to pay the amount of Rs.
14,34,388/- in terms of the memorandum of understanding dated 28th November, 2022.

Petitioners further case is that the opposite party herein filed an application under Section 433,434 and 439 of the Companies Act with a prayer for winding up the company being M/s. Castle Industries Private Limited.

This Hon'ble High Court vide order dated 16th August, 2016 passed in C.P. no. 548 of 2016 had directed the said company to secure a sum of Rs. 10,25,000/- by way of cash security with the Registrar, Original Side, High Court at Calcutta and pursuant to such order,
the company had deposited the said amount by way of cash security.

It is further submitted that during pendency of the company petition, the opposite party and the accused company had entered into a memorandum of understanding on 15th September, 2022 whereby it was agreed that upon receiving the said security amount of Rs. 10,25,000/- along with interest, the party of the second part therein being the company shall pay the interest component received by it to the opposite party herein in full and final satisfaction of the claim of the opposite party.

However, the opposite party herein has deliberately claimed an amount of Rs. 14,34,388/-
without any basis.

It is further submitted that the present petitioner had resigned from the company on 3rd February,
2024 and the cognizance of the present offence was taken on 14th May, 2024.

She further submits that the charges under Section 420/426/120B of the IPC is not maintainable against the present petitioner and the concept of vicarious liability is unknown in the IPC and that no specific act has been attributed to the petitioner herein in showing that the petitioner was in control and management of the company.
Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the application is admitted.
Petitioner is directed to issue process against the opposite party intimating the next date of hearing and to file affidavit of service on the returnable date.

sentences.text:
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and since petition has prima facie make out a case which involves adjudication, let no coercive step be taken against the present petitioner in connection with the aforesaid proceeding till the last date of November, 2025 or until further order,
whichever is earlier.

Let the matter appear on 7th November, 2025 under the "Contested Application".
(Dr. Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee, J.)
